title: terraform-module-integrity - post-deploy orchestrator for API readiness & model smoke
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a reusable post-deploy orchestration step that validates Terraform module outputs and performs fast, deterministic post-deploy health checks for Private (VPC) deployments. This work sits between the IaC apply stage and the existing probe-runner: it verifies that network constructs, IAM/KMS references, DNS entries, and instance metadata match the Terraform state, then exercises API readiness endpoints and performs lightweight model-load smoke flows to detect incorrect image tags, missing model artifacts, or KV-cache warmup failures before marking the deployment healthy.

Scope:
- Terraform module integrity checks: validate state->actual drift for VPC subnets, route tables, security group rules, KMS key ARNs, and output addresses used by the control plane. Fail fast with actionable diffs.
- API readiness step: call internal /healthz, /models/:id/status, token handshake, and a small set of canonical inference requests against the deployed API gateway (with retry/backoff). Capture latencies and error distribution.
- Model smoke/priming flow: run a 3-request warmup sequence per model variant (short prefix, typical-length prompt, and a mem-pressure case) to ensure KV cache loads and that quantized backends return coherent outputs. Use deterministic prompts from the eval suite.
- Orchestration and idempotency: implement as a Terraform null_resource + external script (or Kubernetes Job on private control plane) with clear runbook integration and signal for the deploy pipeline to proceed/rollback. Support a dry-run mode that returns diffs only.

Acceptance criteria:
1) A terraform-integrity script returns non-zero and prints a structured diff when outputs don't match live resources.
2) API readiness step returns HTTP200 for /healthz and reports model status as 'loaded' within 60s for healthy model artifacts.
3) Model smoke flow completes within 90s per model variant and records token-level latency and a simple similarity check against golden outputs.
4) Orchestrator integrates with the deploy pipeline: if any check fails, pipeline blocks and opens ENG ticket with pre-filled diagnostics; if checks pass, pipeline proceeds and marks release tag.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/Private+Post-Deploy+Orchestrator+Spec
- RFC draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/214
- Implementation WIP branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/deploy-scripts/tree/feature/terraform-integrity-orchestrator
- Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-infra/private-deploy-health
- Runbook: gs://redwood-runbooks/vpc-post-deploy-orchestrator.md

Risks and trade-offs considered:
- Running model warmup in the deploy path increases deploy time; mitigations: parallelize per-model variant and provide configurable thresholds to skip non-critical variants.
- Relying on Terraform state can mask drift if state is out-of-date; mitigation: prefer live resource queries for critical checks and surface Terraform state inconsistencies to the operator.
- Secrets/KMS access for smoke tests: use ephemeral deploy credentials scoped to read-only model metadata and inference endpoints; log nothing sensitive.

Next steps (short term):
- Merge RFC, finish terraform null_resource runner (Luca), and land GH action that invokes the orchestrator after terraform apply.
- Add golden prompts for the top 5 customer-facing models to the eval repo and wire similarity threshold configs.

Longer term: consider moving the orchestrator into the control plane as a managed Job that can be re-run independently of the pipeline and report historical pass/fail metrics in Console.

comments: 2026-02-19 - Asha Patel: Initial ticket created after incident post-upgrade where a missing KMS alias caused model load failures. Captured core requirements from incident review.

2026-02-28 - Priya Shah (SRE): Reviewed prototype. Requested explicit CIDR verification and a toggle to skip smoke-tests in low-traffic batches. Suggested storing diffs in S3 for later analysis.
2026-03-03 - Design review (Ben Carter): UX for pipeline blocking should include a one-click rerun and a link to diagnostics. Added UI stub in Console mockups.
